title: RAW UNREVIEWED: a Fortune status family separates tense and privation while actor identity can change
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. Clm4660 f1r writes regnabo/regno/regnavi/sum sine regno around a real wheel: three verbal tense forms share a status nucleus but the fourth is an explicit privative construction. Whole Carmen16 preserves one I through earlier enthronement and present descent, then says alter rises and names Hecuba below. Try one shared status-and-reference grammar across the complete existing f85r2 four blocks, not four proper names or automatic one-person identity. No target alignment or word meaning is claimed.

design.mechanism: A time-indexed status predication keeps the same semantic status argument while future, present, perfect and explicit WITHOUT take different scopes. A second, separate referent rule permits the same speaker to persist across his past/present clauses but switches to another participant only when explicitly licensed; status/office identity is not person identity.
design.unit: All four existing f85r2 spatial blocks: N .2–6, E .7–11, S .12–17, W .18–23, with .1/.24 retained separately and the complete GDT1043 image inventory. Source unit is the whole Clm4660 f1r, not a crop of four labels; complete edited Carmina16,17,18,18a,19 are preserved with their different locations.
design.contrast: A common predicative family with tense/privation and licensed reference change versus four independent stage names, four names of people, or one silently identical person in every picture.
design.prediction: If such a construction is authored, its privative clause must deny present possession of the same status rather than merely place an assertion in the past; a future clause cannot itself assert current possession. A surviving common status form must retain that role after an explicit participant switch. These are obligations of the declared hypothesis, not observations already made in Voynich.
design.scope: A new source-and-construction opportunity only. It does not reopen a literal Laufenberg equation or establish Latin as the target language.

historical_source.inscriptions: Left regnabo; top regno; right regnaui (normalized regnavi, faded native letters); bottom sum sine regno. Edited Carmen18a corroborates the four-part wording.
historical_source.printed_context: Carmen17 compares Fortune to the Moon and addresses a changing wheel. It is not an astronomical assertion that the central figure is the Moon. Carmen16 is separate edited context, not claimed to occur on viewed f1r. The viewed leaf also begins Carmen19; its full edited text is retained, not mislabelled as a wheel caption.
historical_source.identity_counterexample: Carmen16 sederam elatus / nunc a summo corrui / descendo retain the first-person speaker, then alter in altum tollitur explicitly introduces another, and Hecubam reginam supplies a further named referent. No identical crown proves one person throughout.

positive_existing_target_constraints: GDT1042 supplies complete108/107/109 groups in the four blocks; aiin alone is reader-exact in every block, but is not selected as a status, person or tense word. No exact repeated bigram survives in all three readings.

The reusable-part baseline permits a family hypothesis, but GDT915/916 prohibit treating every novel apparent stem pair as already validated composition. No automatic affix deletion or Latin morphology transfer.

GDT1043 supplies four attached torso figures, text sectors and an independently inventoried centre/outer plumes; it does not supply Fortune, a rotation direction, shared person identity or a four-clause reading.
additional_assumptions: That the four entire spatial texts contain status accounts at all; neither their sequence nor one clause per block is observed.
A shared status kernel and written tense/privation operators must still be proposed from actual complete forms; no aiin meaning or free four-label dictionary is installed here.
Any same-person link across target clauses is a declared reference choice, separately costed from a repeated role/status. A replacement person cannot be silently merged with the prior actor.
A medieval source convention may motivate C0 authoring without copying this source. Four figures, crowns or a Moon comparison alone do not identify a Vorlage.
two_discriminating_consequences: After selecting one concrete written status construction, its future and privative versions must yield different current-state assertions; treating every affix as a stage-name alias would lose that distinction.

When the participant changes, the status relation can persist while the personal antecedent changes. An account claiming one person across all four needs written support against the source's explicit alter rival; conversely a four-person reading must still explain any written coreference across past/present clauses.
strongest_known_countercases: ARUNDEL_WHOLE_LABELS_REPORT already separates four ages, ten life episodes, speakers and divine centre. Speaker/role distinctions and first-person royal claims are therefore not new discoveries. The new source input is the explicit regn- tense/privation family, not a generic Fortune-wheel resemblance.

Clm4660 has an actual spoked wheel, ascending/descending/prostrate and enthroned figures, a central crowned person and crown loss; f85r2 has materially different hand objects and outer plumes. No direct template mapping follows.
GDT1042: block lengths19/27/26/36 ZL, reader variants and missing common bigrams. Four short Latin formulas cannot stand in for108 groups. GDT884's specific24 equations remain analytically UNSAT.
Past tense alone does not entail no longer reigning; the loss reading has image/context support, whereas sum sine regno states privation explicitly. Do not collapse those semantics.

GDT998 contradicts all6925 exposed18-group windows for its exact concatenative stem/person/tense table writer. Four Fortune formulas do not reopen that writer, establish a target tense table, or warrant another table search. The source offers a different scoped status/privation construction only if actual whole target contexts support it.
smallest_next_step: Before any target test, author one finite shared status/reference rule manually over all four already-owned blocks, preserving every unknown group and all variants. Choose its written carrier and scopes explicitly, then check that one additional occurrence forces a tense/privation or participant consequence outside the motivating span. If this cannot be done without separately inventing the four predicates, retain the source as RAW and do not build a decoder.
